bonuses.requirements: EU authorities recognize Circle's USDC as 'significant' under MiCA | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsIndepth ResearchEU authorities recognize Circl...EU authorities recognize Circle's USDC as 'significant' under MiCAcryptonews.ruPublished on 2026-10-14Last updated on 2026-10-14AbstractThe European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle's USDC stablecoin as a "significant" electronic money token under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. This designation, shared by only 45 other projects, subjects USDC to joint oversight by the EBA and France's Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. As the world's second-largest stablecoin with a $73 billion market capitalization, USDC's new status comes amid EU-based issuers seeking regulated dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. While European regulators cannot eliminate such dollar-linked tokens, they can enforce protective measures and rules for their issuers.#USDC Price#USDC Regular Invest#USDC Surge#USDC Plunge#Classification#electronic money#EU#European Banking Authority#Market Cap#MiCA#Regulation#Stablecoin#Supervision#USDCThe European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified the $USDC stablecoin from Circle as a significant electronic money token under the European Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) legislation.In a notice published on Wednesday, the banking regulator stated that the electronic money token classification, granted to only 45 other projects, effectively means the $USDC stablecoin will be under the joint supervision of the EBA and the French supervisory authority — the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. The stablecoin ranks second in market capitalization: $73 billion versus $184 billion for Tether USDt.The 'significant' status comes at a time when many EU-based token issuers have been striving for regulated, dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.9%. Technology and AI infrastructure stocks were notably hit, with Bitcoin miners plunging as much as 13%. Companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Oracle saw significant declines.

The selloff extended to Bitcoin mining firms, many of which have expanded into AI infrastructure. TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining, and IREN all dropped over 12%. The downturn is partly attributed to concerns that higher interest rates could increase borrowing costs for data center expansion.

September's U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year-over-year, exceeding forecasts and the Fed's 2% target, largely due to higher gasoline prices. bonuses.requirements: Bloomberg: Daiwa Securities and Mizuho Obtain Wholly-Owned Licenses in Mainland ChinaHomeFeedNewsBloomberg: Daiwa Securities and Mizuho Obtain Wholly-Owned Licenses in Mainland ChinaBloomberg: Daiwa Securities and Mizuho Obtain Wholly-Owned Licenses in Mainland China10/20 04:30According to Bloomberg citing sources, Japan's Daiwa Securities Group and Mizuho Financial Group have been notified that they can conduct wholly-owned securities business in mainland China. The relevant approvals were advanced after Vice Premier He Lifeng hosted a senior Japanese trade delegation in March this year to discuss expanding bilateral trade and cross-border investment. A spokesperson for Mizuho Securities confirmed the news, stating that preparations for opening are ongoing, while a spokesperson for Daiwa Securities declined to comment. Daiwa Securities was approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission in 2021 to establish a joint venture securities company with a 51% stake. In April this year, it spent approximately $100 million to acquire the remaining shares from its Chinese partner, and last week it was approved to complete the equity change, achieving full ownership. Mizuho Securities was approved in October 2025 to establish a wholly-owned securities company, and after completing on-site inspections and operational reviews by regulatory authorities, it was issued a securities business license last week.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。All Comments0LatestHotLatestHotTrending Topics

Real-time news, insights, prices, trending stories, and expert analysis - all in one place.Is 2008 Happening Again? CDS Returns to the Market SpotlightAI debt bubble concerns are driving an explosive surge in credit default swap (CDS) trading, echoing the pre-2008 financial crisis era. According to Morgan Stanley, weekly average CDS trading volume tied to Oracle, SpaceX, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Broadcom, and Nvidia exceeded $9 billion in September, up over 4.5x from under $2 billion in July. Goldman Sachs data shows AI single-name CDS volume grew 400% year-over-year, with liquid names expanding from 4 to 10-12. AI-related companies have issued about $466 billion in bonds in 2026, up over 3.6x from $101 billion a year earlier. Prices signal stress: Meta 5-year CDS hit a record 108bps, Nvidia 101bps, Oracle jumped from 144bps to 322bps, and SpaceX doubled to 226bps. Investors increasingly prefer CDS over stock put options, which are costly and difficult for hedging hyperscaler risk. CoreWeave is the most vulnerable name, with 5-year CDS around 1090bps, implying a 63% five-year default probability. Goldman warns new debt issuance and SPV structures will keep generating hedging demand, while financial and insurance sector CDS are also being sought amid concentration risk concerns.marsbit17m agomarsbit17m agoCICC: Can the AI boom withstand the supply test?Global AI supply chains diverged after a Q3 correction eased crowding. Taiwan's index and Nasdaq hit new highs, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, STAR 50, and ChiNext 50 stalled or gave back gains. Beyond macro factors, this reflects shifting supply-demand dynamics: cloud capex growth may have peaked, new applications are slow to arrive, and upstream supply (optical modules, GPUs, memory) is being released, narrowing the supply gap and challenging the "volume-price upcycle" narrative.
